title: Counting the uncountable: sketches for huge data
dek: How many different people saw this ad today? Which dishes are trending this hour? What is the p99 latency across 200 servers? Exact answers need memory that grows with the data. Sketches answer in a few kilobytes with a small, known error, and they merge, so each server or hour can keep its own.

items: Counting distinct customers exactly means remembering every ID you've seen: 1 crore IDs is about 80 MB, per ad, per day.
Counting how often each dish is ordered needs a counter per dish, and the 'top 10' needs all of them sorted.
Percentiles need every latency value, or at least a sorted sample, and they can't be averaged across servers.
At small scale, do it exactly. Sketches pay off when the counts are many, wide or spread across machines.

body.cap: The longest run of zeros in a hash is a noisy clue to how many distinct items were hashed; averaging thousands of such clues makes it a precise one.

body.label: ZOTATO · DISTINCT VIEWERS OF AN AD, IN REDIS
body.x:
PFADD ad:7:2026-11-08 u77 u12 u903     # add viewers (repeats change nothing)
PFCOUNT ad:7:2026-11-08                 # about how many distinct viewers
PFMERGE ad:7:week ad:7:2026-11-02 ad:7:2026-11-03 ad:7:2026-11-04 ad:7:2026-11-05 ad:7:2026-11-06 ad:7:2026-11-07 ad:7:2026-11-08
body.say: Redis HyperLogLog commands. Add viewer IDs to the sketch for ad 7 today; adding a repeat changes nothing. Count about how many distinct viewers. Merge the seven daily sketches into one for the week.

body.cap: Collisions can only add to a counter, never subtract, so the smallest of a dish's counters is the closest to the truth.

items: Keep a small heap of the current top items alongside the sketch to answer 'the 10 most ordered dishes this hour'.
Error is relative to the total: with 2,718 counters per row and 5 rows, an estimate is within 0.1% of all orders, 99% of the time. Big items are accurate; tiny ones are noise.
It suits trending lists, abuse detection (which IPs are hammering us) and cache admission decisions.

items: When the question says 'unique', 'top', 'trending' or 'percentile' at large scale, offer the sketch and its error.
Say they merge: per-shard or per-minute sketches, combined for the dashboard.
Keep exact counts where money is involved (billing, payouts) and sketches for the rest.
Where it appears here: Ad clicks counts distinct viewers with HyperLogLog; Web crawler and Dating swipes use Bloom filters to skip what's been seen.

body.x: A random hash starts with one zero half the time, two zeros a quarter of the time, k zeros once in 2^k. If the longest run you have seen is 20, you have probably hashed about 10 lakh distinct items. One such clue is wildly noisy, so HyperLogLog splits hashes into 16,384 buckets by their first bits, keeps the longest run per bucket, and combines them with a harmonic mean, which keeps a few lucky buckets from dominating. Repeats hash the same way, so they never change a register: that is why it counts distinct items, not events.
